findings.evidence: Table 6-1's Decode row puts the verdict in a column headed "H100 capacity" containing "~3.35 TB/s HBM (single-device)" and a "Verdict" cell that says "memory-bound by intensity (~1.0 FLOP/byte ≪ ridge ~295); weight-read bandwidth is not binding at the canonical point — 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9% achieved HBM util".
findings.issue: The table's own verdict column simultaneously asserts "memory-bound" and "weight-read bandwidth is not binding" without flagging that these are two different senses of the word (roofline regime vs. achieved-utilization shortfall). The same cell carries both a batch-1 single-device signature and the TP=8 host signature, which is the exact conflation the chapter's §6.3.3 prose warns against ("This 5.6-vs-3.35 TB/s comparison is an illustrative single-device roofline argument, not the canonical 8×H100 host's actual deployment verdict").
findings.fix_instruction: Split the Decode verdict cell into two explicitly named rows or sub-rows — "regime (roofline)" and "achieved HBM utilization on the canonical host" — and state in the cell that the 5.6-vs-3.35 TB/s comparison applies to the hypothetical single-device case only.

findings.evidence: The figure box prints "Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency", and the caption concedes: "the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric."
findings.issue: A known erratum is shipped in the figure and corrected only in the caption. §6.1.1 and Ch. 4 §4.3 both insist concurrency is a derived serving-side quantity, so the figure contradicts the chapter's own taxonomy on its first page.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-render Fig. 6.1 with the workload box reading "rps (λ) · token profile" only, and delete the caption erratum note once the art is corrected.

findings.evidence: Section 6.3.4 reads: "aggregate prefill demand at the 40 rps peak is 40 × 1.29 ≈ 51.6 PFLOP/s against the 8×H100 sustained prefill capacity of ~2.77 PFLOP/s (35% MFU, Ch 8 §3) — ~18.6× oversubscribed (the datasheet-peak ~7.9 PFLOPS gives ~6.5×, a theoretical ceiling only; under case (ii), full-square attention, the same 40 rps traffic peak at the same 35% MFU planning rate screens ~22 hosts — Ch 8 §3), consistent with Ch 8's 19-host screen at this peak (case (i))". The §6.8 mini-case then states: "case (i)'s prefill screen needs ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts, but the KV-residency / Little's-Law screen needs ⌈344/17⌉ = 21 hosts at the peak and therefore binds (Ch 8 §3; Ch 17)". The host reference 'Ch 8 §3' is therefore used for four distinct quantities in two chapters — the 19-host case-(i) screen, the ~22-host case-(ii) screen, the ~2.77 PFLOP/s capacity figure, and the 35% MFU planning rate — with no figure or table number given for any of them, even though Chapter 8's Table 8-1 is the natural anchor for the prefill rate and the case-(i)/(ii)/(iii) convention is defined in Ch 2 Table 2-2's scope note and Ch 8 §3.3.
findings.issue: Cross-references to 'Ch 8 §3' are used as the sole authority for four different numeric results across Ch 6 (§6.3.4 and §6.8), including a 19-host screen, a 22-host screen, a 2.77 PFLOP/s capacity and a 35% MFU planning rate, with no figure/table pointer — so a reader cannot verify which specific artefact carries each number without reading all of Ch 8 §3.
findings.fix_instruction: Give each of the four Ch 8-sourced quantities in §6.3.4 and §6.8 a specific pointer (e.g. 'Ch 8 §3, Table 8-1' for the ~2.77 PFLOP/s planning capacity and the 35% MFU assumption, and 'Ch 8 §3 case (i) / case (ii)' for the 19- and 22-host screens), so the referenced targets can be resolved individually.

findings.evidence: Figure art text layer prints: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The caption states the line is "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget". Ch 4 (printed p. 86) is emphatic: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to".
findings.issue: The art labels the 2 s line '(TTFT budget)', contradicting the book's load-bearing budget-vs-ceiling terminology (1.2 s = design budget; 2 s = p95 ceiling). The caption corrects the semantics but never acknowledges that the art itself carries the wrong term, so a reader of the figure alone internalizes exactly the conflation the Preface forbids ('load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed').
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the figure's SLO line to 'SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)' (or 'p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s'); caption can then stand unchanged.

findings.evidence: Art text layer: "Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency". §6.1.1: "Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law)... Fig 6.1's workload box therefore carries only offered quantities — the request rate λ (rps) and the token profile." Caption: "the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric."
findings.issue: The workload box of the chapter's spine figure prints 'concurrency' as a workload metric, contradicting §6.1.1's classification (concurrency is serving-side, derived like queue depth). The caption admits the erratum, but the shipped art still carries the wrong label, so figure and body text disagree.
findings.fix_instruction: Correct the figure art: replace the third entry 'concurrency' with 'request rate λ' (or delete it) so the box matches §6.1.1; the caption's erratum note can then be removed.

findings.evidence: Table 6-1, Decode row, Resource tell column: "(ii) Canonical 8×H100, TP=8 operating point: low-to-moderate HBM util (~21% of 3.35 TB/s), so HBM saturation is not the tell here"
findings.issue: The resource tell for the canonical host in Table 6-1 incorrectly lists low HBM utilization as a diagnostic signal for a memory-bound regime. Low utilization is a symptom of the tensor-parallel sharding (where the weight read is distributed), not an indicator of the underlying roofline regime (memory-bound). This contradicts the text in §2.3 and §6.3.3, which explicitly state that the bandwidth-bound verdict comes from arithmetic intensity (~1 FLOP/byte), not from the device utilization rate. A reader looking for high HBM utilization to confirm 'memory-bound' on an 8xH100 host will not find it.
findings.fix_instruction: Clarify that 'low HBM util' is an artifact of the TP=8 distribution, and that the 'tell' for this regime on the canonical host is actually the high ratio of memory-read latency to compute time, or TP-collective overhead, rather than the raw bandwidth percentage. Alternatively, restrict this 'tell' to the single-device hypothetical row to avoid confusion.

findings.chapter: Chapter 6 — Measuring What Matters: From Telemetry to Architecture Decisions
findings.evidence: Figure art: "Workload metrics rps · token profile · concurrency". Caption: "Figure-art note: the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric."
findings.issue: The rendered figure still labels concurrency as a workload metric, while §6.1.1 and the caption state that concurrency is derived on the serving side and the offered request rate λ belongs in the workload box. This is a figure-versus-text mismatch visible to readers.
findings.fix_instruction: Regenerate Figure 6.1 so the workload box reads "rps · token profile · λ" (or equivalent offered-load wording), remove "concurrency" from that box, and then delete the now-unnecessary figure-art erratum note from the caption.
